THE CHALLENGE
The Problem
Why pregnancy AI needs a new approach
810
women die daily from preventable pregnancy complications globally
94%
of maternal deaths occur in LMICs where antenatal care access is limited
3
critical barriers in all existing maternal AI systems

⚠ Single-outcome focus

Most systems target one condition. Pregnancy is multi-dimensional — PPD, preterm birth, and preeclampsia co-occur and share risk factors.

⚠ LLM hallucination risk

Özer Aslan et al. [2025] showed major chatbots produce clinically inaccurate maternal health guidance without evidence grounding.

⚠ No actionable output

ML risk scores without conversational guidance have limited utility for patients without medical training.

MaternaAI — Mentor Presentation · March 2026
OVERVIEW
What is MaternaAI?
A full-stack perinatal AI companion

MaternaAI is the first system to combine RAG clinical grounding, multi-outcome ML risk scoring, and LLM reasoning in a single deployable pregnancy companion — addressing all three barriers simultaneously.

7 Clinical Modules
🩺 Symptom Checker 📅 Due Date 🥗 Nutrition Guide 👶 Kick Counter ⏱ Contractions 📔 Mood + EPDS 📊 Risk Dashboard
Gemini 3.1 Pro

SYSTEM DESIGN
Architecture
Four-layer design with parallel AI branches
Layer 1
Input
Free-text symptom message + structured patient context profile
Layer 2
Processing
RAG retriever + ML risk scorer running in parallel
Layer 3
Reasoning
Gemini 3.1 Pro — enriched prompt with clinical KB + risk scores
Layer 4
Output
URGENT/WATCH/NORMAL · Explanation · Actions · Red flags

RAG PIPELINE
Clinical Grounding
ACOG-grounded RAG to prevent LLM hallucination
Knowledge Base
8 entries from ACOG Practice Bulletins Nos. 189, 202, 222, 229, 234
Encoder
sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 · 384-dim L2-normalised dense vectors
Retrieval
Cosine similarity · Top-K = 2 · Relevance threshold = 0.30
Why RAG?
Özer Aslan et al. and Al-Haideri et al. [2025] showed general LLMs produce clinically inaccurate maternal health guidance without grounding
Prompt
KB text + ML risk scores + gestational week → Gemini 3.1 Pro

RESULTS
Feature Importance
What drives each risk prediction?
BMI dominates all 3 models
Strongest shared predictor (0.190 PPD, 0.144 preeclampsia) — adiposity-mediated pathway
Systolic BP → Preeclampsia
Highest single importance score (0.170) — aligns with diagnostic criteria for hypertensive disorders
Gestational week → Preterm
Top predictor for preterm (0.155) — timing defines clinical urgency
Depression history → PPD
3rd strongest PPD predictor (0.147) — confirms clinical literature on recurrence risk

Literature (high-resource) MaternaAI (clinical features only)

Intentional trade-off

MaternaAI uses only routinely collectible clinical + SDOH features available in LMICs — not lab data.

Literature gap

High-AUC models [0.78–0.85] require plasma proteomics, microbiome sequencing, or extensive EHR histories — all LMIC-incompatible.

Comparable baseline

Within low-resource feature constraints, MaternaAI performs comparably to PIERS-ML (10 variables) on preeclampsia.

DISCUSSION
Key Findings
What we learned from building and evaluating MaternaAI
01

RAG grounding works

Cosine similarity retrieval at threshold 0.30 anchors Gemini responses to ACOG guidelines — directly addressing the hallucination problem documented by Özer Aslan et al. [2025].

02

BMI is a universal predictor

BMI emerged as the strongest shared feature across all three models — suggesting a common adiposity-mediated pathway worth further clinical investigation.

03

Low-resource models are viable

AUC 0.58–0.66 using only routine clinical + SDOH features compares favourably to PIERS-ML. MaternaAI's accuracy/deployability trade-off is clinically justified.

04

EPDS in conversation increases uptake

Embedding the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale within a conversational flow aligns with evidence from Daly et al. [2025] on improved perinatal screening engagement.

MaternaAI — Mentor Presentation · March 2026
DISCUSSION
Limitations
Honest gaps — what we have not yet solved
Synthetic training data
Models trained on CDC PRAMS-structured synthetic data, not real patient records. External validation required.
Small KB (8 entries)
RAG knowledge base covers 8 ACOG topics. Rare conditions (HELLP, placenta accreta) not covered.
Gemini API dependency
Requires internet + Google API key — incompatible with offline LMIC rural settings.
No clinical review
Triage outputs not reviewed by registered midwives or obstetricians. Clinical validation study pending.
Threshold sensitivity
Sensitivity at default 0.5 threshold is low for PPD (9.8%) — threshold tuning for recall-priority needed.
No real user study
Patient engagement, satisfaction, and adherence not yet measured in a prospective study.

FUTURE SCOPE
6 Research Directions
What comes next for MaternaAI
🌐

Federated Learning

Privacy-preserving model training across LMIC clinical sites — no patient data leaves the facility.

High priority
📱

On-device LLM

Deploy Gemma 2B via ONNX Runtime for offline inference — critical for rural LMIC settings.

High priority
📚

Expanded RAG KB

Scale from 8 to 50+ entries covering rare complications, postpartum care, and multi-language support.

Medium priority
📊

Longitudinal tracking

Week-by-week risk trajectories to detect deterioration before acute symptoms emerge.

Medium priority
👨

Partner PPD

Extend ML + EPDS to paternal postpartum depression — a completely untouched AI research gap.

Novel direction
🏥

Clinical validation

200-query prospective study with registered midwife review — required for regulatory credibility.

Essential next step
